slot.brief: A particle moving in a straight line at constant velocity; find angular momentum about a point off its path and show/verify whether it stays constant.

stem: A particle of mass $2\ \text{kg}$ is at $(2\hat{\mathbf i}+\hat{\mathbf j})\ \text{m}$ at $t=0$ and moves with constant velocity $(3\hat{\mathbf i}+4\hat{\mathbf j})\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Which expression gives its angular momentum about the origin at time $t$ (in seconds)?

verdicts.working: \(\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v\), with \(\mathbf r=(2+3t)\hat{\mathbf i}+(1+4t)\hat{\mathbf j}\) and \(m\mathbf v=6\hat{\mathbf i}+8\hat{\mathbf j}\). Thus \(L_z=(2+3t)8-(1+4t)6=10\).

working:
$\vec r(t)=[(2+3t)\hat{\mathbf i}+(1+4t)\hat{\mathbf j}]\,\text{m}$; $\vec p=(6\hat{\mathbf i}+8\hat{\mathbf j})\,\text{kg m s}^{-1}$; $\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p=[8(2+3t)-6(1+4t)]\hat{\mathbf k}=10\hat{\mathbf k}\,\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$, independent of $t$.

Independent check: \(\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times m\mathbf v\), with \(\mathbf r=(2+3t)\hat{\mathbf i}+(1+4t)\hat{\mathbf j}\) and \(m\mathbf v=6\hat{\mathbf i}+8\hat{\mathbf j}\). Thus \(L_z=(2+3t)8-(1+4t)6=10\).
